{
  "research_question": "Does intracortical microstimulation (ICMS) combined with visual cues improve mouse navigation performance compared to unimodal stimulation (ICMS-only or visual-only) or sham stimulation, and which performance variables best discriminate among stimulation paradigms?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "Use Welch's ANOVA if variance homogeneity is violated, as sample sizes are highly unbalanced (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505)",
    "For binary Success (0/1), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than standard ANOVA, treating Stim Paradigm as predictor",
    "Check effect sizes (eta-squared or partial eta-squared) given the large sample sizes where trivial differences may achieve statistical significance",
    "Include Mouse as a blocking factor or random effect in mixed-effects models to account for 8 mice with repeated measures"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous outcomes with significant ANOVA: pairwise comparisons with Games-Howell test (unequal variances) or Tukey-Kramer (equal variances) among the 5 paradigms",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs ICMS Only, Combined vs Bright Visual Only, Combined vs Dim Visual Only, Combined vs Sham, and multimodal vs unimodal pooled",
    "For binary Success: pairwise proportion tests with confidence intervals, or marginal means from logistic regression with multiplicity adjustment",
    "Dunnett's procedure for comparing all active conditions against Sham control",
    "Estimate standardized mean differences (Cohen's d) for all pairwise comparisons to assess practical significance"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control across all tests within each response variable family; additionally control family-wise error across the five response variables using Holm-Bonferroni or hierarchical gatekeeping, prioritizing Success and Time-to-Target as primary endpoints",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression or gradient-boosted classifier (e.g., XGBoost, LightGBM) with Stim Paradigm as the categorical response and the five performance variables as predictors. This is recommended over forced linear regression because: (1) the response is categorical with no natural ordering, (2) decision boundaries among paradigms are likely nonlinear, and (3) class imbalance (Combined 63.7% vs Sham 4.6%) requires stratified sampling or class-weighting. Random forest with Mouse held out as test set provides robust cross-validation for generalization across animals. If ordinality can be justified (Sham < unimodal < multimodal), an ordinal logistic regression or proportional odds model could be tested but requires validation of proportional odds assumption.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals; consider Box-Cox transformation for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency given right skew (max values 201.4 and 29.8 vs means ~2.8 and 0.47)",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Levene's test; expect violation due to Sham showing markedly higher variance in Time-to-Target and lower Success variance",
    "Independence: Assess autocorrelation in repeated trials within mice using Durbin-Watson or mixed-effects structure",
    "Collinearity among predictors: VIF < 5 for multinomial logistic regression; Success and Path Efficiency may correlate strongly",
    "Sample size adequacy: Rule of thumb 10-20 events per predictor for multinomial logit; adequate given n=76655 but sparse cells for Sham (n=3505) may limit precision for that class",
    "Complete separation check in logistic models for Success, especially for Sham vs others"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation will show highest Success (~0.78) and lowest Time-to-Target (~2.56s), significantly outperforming Sham (Success ~0.27, Time-to-Target ~4.68s)",
    "Bright Visual Only will outperform Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only, approaching Combined performance, confirming visual salience effects",
    "Sham will show lowest Path Efficiency (~0.31) and AD (~0.24), indicating more erratic, less directed trajectories",
    "AD (angular dispersion) will discriminate multimodal from unimodal conditions, with Combined showing highest AD (~0.40) suggesting more exploratory but efficient search patterns",
    "Average Speed differences will be modest (10.7-12.8 units) and may not survive multiplicity correction, suggesting speed-accuracy trade-off is not the primary strategy",
    "Multinomial classifier will achieve highest accuracy distinguishing Sham from all others; confusion expected between Combined and Bright Visual Only",
    "Mouse effects will explain substantial variance, requiring random effects or stratified validation"
  ],
  "limitations": "Highly unbalanced design with Combined comprising 63.7% of data and Sham only 4.6%, leading to imprecise estimates for rare classes and potential bias toward majority class in predictive models; unknown trial sequence and learning effects not captured in summary statistics; AD interpretation as angular dispersion assumes planar navigation geometry not verified; no information on trial duration limits or timeout criteria affecting Time-to-Target censoring; missing covariates (day of testing, previous trial outcome) that could explain within-mouse variation; cross-sectional summary statistics preclude modeling of temporal dynamics or trial-level dependencies",
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit mixed-effects models with crossed or nested random effects for Mouse and session/day if available, using Stim Paradigm as fixed effect; implement multinomial logistic regression with elastic net regularization for paradigm prediction followed by SHAP value analysis to rank variable importance; conduct targeted subgroup analysis on the 3,505 Sham trials versus matched samples from other conditions to verify effect replication; if trial-level timestamps exist, model learning curves and test for paradigm × trial number interactions to assess whether observed differences reflect stable performance or acquisition rates"
}
